Yong Seung-ho (Korean: 용승호), better known by his stage name Seungri (승리), is a South Korean singer, songwriter, record producer, actor, and entrepreneur. He was born on December 12, 1990, in Gwangju, South Korea. Seungri is best known as a former member of the South Korean boy band Big Bang, which was formed by YG Entertainment in 2006.

Seungri was the youngest member of Big Bang and was known for his dancing, rapping, and singing skills. He also had a significant role in the group's songwriting and production. Over the years, Seungri released several solo projects, including the EPs "V.V.I.P" (2011) and "Let's Talk About Love" (2013), and the album "The Great Seungri" (2018).

Apart from his music career, Seungri has also acted in various television dramas and films, such as "Why Did You Come to My House?" (2009) and "Angel Eyes" (2014). He has also been involved in several variety shows, showcasing his personality and humor.

Seungri has been involved in various business ventures, including opening a nightclub in Gangnam, Seoul, called "Burning Sun." However, in early 2019, he became embroiled in a scandal involving the club, which was accused of various illegal activities, including drug use, sexual assault, and police corruption. As a result of the scandal, Seungri announced his retirement from the entertainment industry on March 11, 2019.

Following his retirement, Seungri faced multiple legal charges, including procuring prostitutes for foreign investors, embezzlement, and violation of the Food Sanitation Act. In August 2021, he was found guilty by a South Korean military court of several charges, including embezzlement, procuring prostitutes, and overseas gambling, and was sentenced to three years in prison. He is currently serving his sentence.

Yong Sung Ki is a Korean actor and martial artist, primarily recognized for his roles in action and martial arts films. He was born on March 15, 1949, in Busan, South Korea.

Yong Sung Ki began his martial arts training in Taekwondo at a young age, achieving the rank of 9th dan grandmaster in the art. He later went on to train in Hapkido, Kuk Sool Won, and Judo.

In the late 1960s, Yong Sung Ki moved to the United States where he started his acting career in martial arts films. Some of his most notable appearances include roles in "Five Fingers of Death" (1972), "The Invincible Kim dynasty" (1973), and "The Master Django" (1988).

In addition to his acting career, Yong Sung Ki has also opened several martial arts schools around the world and continues to teach and promote martial arts. He is often referred to as the "Father of American Taekwondo."
